title: Building an offer that justifies a higher rate for residential cleaning
audience: Owners of residential cleaning businesses, including solo operators, who quote regular and deep cleans for homes and need to explain a higher price.
learningOutcomes: Write an offer with a clear promised outcome, time frame and conditions
Identify the friction and risk the customer carries and reduce them
Price the offer on value and cost, not only time

instruction.heading: A bad offer versus a good offer for a home clean
instruction.body: 'I clean houses' is a service. 'I will leave the kitchen, bathrooms and floors done to a written checklist within the time we agree, send photos of the checklist at sign-off, and return within a set window to redo any listed item that is missed' is an offer. The household buys a home that feels ready and the time it gets back, plus the certainty that the checklist has been done.

instruction.heading: The five parts of a home clean offer
instruction.body: Set the outcome (the rooms and tasks, named on a checklist), the time frame (on-site hours you have measured on past cleans), what the household must do (access, pets secured, benchtops cleared), the certainty you give (checklist, photos, sign-off) and the risk you carry (the return visit). Put the scope and exclusions in writing, such as the inside of the oven or the inside of cupboards, because a written quote becomes binding once it is accepted (business.gov.au, 1 August 2025).

instruction.heading: Stepped packages for a home
instruction.body: A good-better-best layout suits home cleaning. The base level is the standard checklist, the middle level adds one task the household can see, and the top level adds a set list of deep-clean jobs. Jobber's Academy shows house cleaning as one trade example of this format (published May 2021, updated 8 October 2024). Set each level's price from your measured hours. Show one total, and say whether GST is included, as the Western Australian guidance asks (WA Consumer Protection, 4 September 2026, WA only).

instruction.heading: Guarantees for a home clean
instruction.body: A return visit to fix listed items is a guarantee you can control, provided your calendar can hold it. Under the consumer guarantees a business must be given a reasonable chance to fix a minor fault free of charge (Consumer Victoria's guidance, 13 October 2023; a Victorian page, so check your state's consumer agency). That page sets no fix window, so set yours and test it on real jobs. A 'no refunds' line does not override a household's rights for services (business.gov.au, 27 May 2025). Do not promise a 'sanitised' or 'germ-free' home unless you can show evidence for it.

instruction.heading: Pricing on value, checked against cost
instruction.body: Price from the outcome and the risk, then check the total against your costs and hours. The marketplace reference for a regular clean is an hourly rate by bedroom count: $80 for a studio, $120 for two bedrooms and $140 for three (Airtasker, Airbnb cleaning page, 27 August 2025). That page was used because Airtasker's house-cleaning page could not be read, so treat it as a vendor reference only. A premium is justified when the household can see the checklist, the photos and the return visit. Gap: the research found no Australian source for a residential minimum charge, and none for referral or repeat rates.

procedure: Write the household's outcome in one sentence that a client would repeat, tied to a named checklist.
Use the on-site times from several past regular cleans to set the time frame for each bedroom count.
List what the household must do, such as clearing benchtops, securing pets and giving access, and reduce each step.
Add one certainty element: a printed checklist, photos at sign-off or a signed sheet.
Set the return-visit window and check that your calendar can hold it.
Price from measured hours and cost, then compare with the marketplace reference and write down which one you used.

workedExamples.situation: A solo residential cleaner in Melbourne (illustrative) keeps losing regular clients to a marketplace listing that shows a bare hourly rate. Households say they cannot tell what the clean includes.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Rewrite the offer for a fortnightly three-bedroom clean, and decide whether a higher price can be defended.
workedExamples.reasoning: The cleaner writes a fortnightly offer with a named checklist covering kitchen, bathrooms, floors and accessible dusting, a photo of the checklist at sign-off, a return visit within a window the cleaner can keep, and a short list of what the household clears before the visit. The marketplace reference for a three-bedroom home is $140 an hour (Airtasker, 27 August 2025). That figure is a comparison point only. The price is set from the cleaner's measured hours and cost, which are worked out in the BP-05 lesson, and the offer does not claim any health outcome.

commonErrors.error: Selling a clean by the hour with no checklist, so the household cannot see what the rate buys.
commonErrors.prevention: Name the rooms and tasks, attach the checklist to the quote and state the return-visit window.
Describe the tasks you perform, not a health outcome. Use only results you can show.

commonErrors.error: Offering a return-visit window that you cannot staff.
commonErrors.prevention: Set the window from your own calendar and count the return visits you can really afford.

commonErrors.error: Relying on a 'no refunds' line to avoid a household's rights.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep the consumer guarantees in your terms and offer a fix-first policy (business.gov.au, 27 May 2025).

commonErrors.error: Treating the marketplace hourly figure as the market rate.
commonErrors.prevention: Note that the figure is a vendor reference from an Airbnb cleaning page, then price from your own costs and hours.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Business guidance only. This lesson does not grant a cleaning licence, registration or insurance. Licence and insurance rules for house cleaning were not researched, so check the rules for your state or territory before you offer the service.

Price display: show one total and say whether GST is included. Business.gov.au says displayed prices should show the total price including GST (18 January 2024). Western Australian guidance asks for the same, and applies in Western Australia only.
The consumer guarantees for services cannot be removed by contract. Check your state's consumer agency for the local rules, because the Victorian page cited here does not cover the other states.

qualityStandard: Offer and pricing decisions are written down and checked against cost and time.
documentationEvidence: Written offer or plan, evidence collected, and the decision made.
summary: A household buys a clean it can see: a named checklist, a time frame, its own part to play and a return visit.
Set the price from measured hours and cost. The marketplace hourly figure is a comparison only.
Gaps: no Australian source for a residential minimum charge, referral rates or house-cleaning licence rules was found. Check these before you publish a guarantee.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which part of a home clean offer does the household buy?
options: Your hourly rate on its own
The outcome, with a checklist and a return visit
How many years you have been in business

knowledgeChecks.question: Why should a home clean guarantee be limited to a return visit?
options: It is the only guarantee the law allows
It is something you control and can staff, so you can afford it
It removes the consumer guarantees for the household
It means you never need a checklist

knowledgeChecks.question: A marketplace shows a per-hour price for three-bedroom homes. What should you do before you quote?
options: Copy the figure exactly, because it is the market rate
Note that it is a vendor reference, then price from your own measured hours and cost
Use the lowest figure you can find on any website
Skip the quote and wait for the household to ask

sourceReferences: business.gov.au, 'Prepare quotes', https://business.gov.au/people/contractors/prepare-quotes, last updated 1 August 2025. Supports: a written quote becomes binding once accepted; a quote should recover cost plus a margin.

WA Consumer Protection, 'Ask us: Estimates and quotes', https://consumerprotection.wa.gov.au/publications/ask-us-estimates-and-quotes, last updated 18 November 2024. Western Australia only. Supports: a quote is a fixed price and an estimate can move; extra work needs the customer's permission; a written quote should state the job, possible extra costs, materials, labour and time to finish.

WA Consumer Protection, 'Estimates, quotes and deposits', https://www.consumerprotection.wa.gov.au/estimates-quotes-and-deposits, last updated 4 September 2026. Western Australia only. Supports: show the total including GST and say whether GST is included; a deposit should generally be no more than 10 per cent; extra work needs written approval.

business.gov.au, 'Warranties and refunds', https://www.business.gov.au/Products-and-services/Fair-trading/Warranties-and-refunds, last updated 27 May 2025. Supports: an optional warranty sits on top of the consumer guarantees; a 'no refunds' line does not override a customer's rights for services.

Consumer Victoria, 'Services not done with due care and skill', https://www.consumer.vic.gov.au/products-and-services/problem-with-a-service/services-not-done-with-due-care-and-skill, last updated 13 October 2023. Victoria. Supports: a business should be given a reasonable chance to fix a minor fault free of charge; the page sets no fix-window length.

Jobber Academy, 'Good, Better, Best Pricing Examples', https://getjobber.com/academy/good-better-best-pricing-examples/, published May 2021, updated 8 October 2024. Older source, updated after 2022. Supports: stepped packages where each higher level adds something the customer can see; house cleaning is one trade example.
business.gov.au, 'Display prices', https://business.gov.au/legal/fair-trading/display-prices, page metadata 18 January 2024. Supports: displayed prices should show the total price, including GST.

Airtasker, 'Airbnb cleaning service cost', https://www.airtasker.com/au/costs/airbnb-cleaning/airbnb-cleaning-service-cost, last updated 27 August 2025. Vendor marketplace; the house-cleaning page could not be read. Supports: hourly rates by bedroom count, per-room prices, a regular clean range of $80 to $180, and a guest fee range of $50 to $300 per booking.

Notes: the figures $80, $120 and $140 are the vendor's hourly rates by bedroom count from the Airbnb cleaning page; the three-hour and marketplace comparisons are illustrative. Source list drawn from team4-V-residential-bond-cleaning.md and team4-R-sol03-tactics.md.
